key_insight: Decoder-based generative LLMs can be used as meaning-aware evaluators for ASR, offering a complementary alternative to surface-based metrics like WER by reasoning about semantic similarity and preference between hypotheses.
problem_solved: Standard ASR metrics (e.g., WER) ignore meaning and poorly match human judgments; this work explores whether generative LLMs can provide more semantically aligned evaluation signals.
method: Pairwise preference: ask a generative LLM to choose the better transcription between two ASR hypotheses.
Generative embeddings: derive semantic distance scores from LLM outputs/embeddings to quantify meaning-level differences between hypothesis and reference.
Qualitative classification: use LLMs to assign semantic error classes or explanations to better characterize mistakes beyond token-level errors.
impact: Provides practitioners with practical, LLM-based tools to evaluate ASR systems in a way that better reflects semantic correctness and human perception, enabling more targeted model improvements and meaningful progress tracking.
visual_elements: Side-by-side example: audio waveform → two transcriptions → LLM preference arrow (shows choice and rationale).
Bar chart comparing correlation with human judgments: WER vs. embedding-based metrics vs. LLM-based scores.
Pipeline diagram: audio → ASR hypotheses → LLM (pairwise / embeddings / classification) → semantic score / error labels.
Heatmap or distance matrix showing generative-embedding distances between multiple hypotheses and the reference.
paper_title: Evaluation of Automatic Speech Recognition Using Generative Large Language Models
paper_authors: Thibault Bañeras-Roux, Shashi Kumar, Driss Khalil, Sergio Burdisso, Petr Motlicek
